purpose: Candidate events for dates that are already occupied in data/events.json. These are source-backed reserve entries for future support of alternate facts, regional editions, topic packs, or a deeper archive.

candidates.title: Wikipedia turns editing into infrastructure
candidates.summary: Wikipedia launched as a freely editable online encyclopedia. It converted wiki-style collaboration into a public knowledge infrastructure that could grow through distributed maintenance.
candidates.lesson: Open systems still need architecture: versioning, moderation, norms and rollback tools can make uncontrolled contributions useful.
candidates.notes: Wikimedia source confirms Jan. 15, 2001 launch. Conflicts with Boston Molasses Flood on 01-15.

candidates.title: LEGO patents a reusable physical interface
candidates.summary: The LEGO Group filed a patent application for the stud-and-tube toy building element. The coupling geometry turned simple plastic bricks into a precise, reusable construction system.
candidates.lesson: A simple interface becomes powerful when tolerances, retention and repeatability let small parts combine into many stable configurations.
candidates.notes: Strong official source; conflicts with Challenger on 01-28.

candidates.title: MRO arrives to make Mars observable in detail
candidates.summary: NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter entered Mars orbit. After aerobraking and checkout, it became high-resolution mapping and communications-relay infrastructure for Mars exploration.
candidates.lesson: Orbit insertion is only the first interface; the real system value comes from instruments, relay links and long operational life.
candidates.notes: NASA source confirms Mars Orbit Insertion on Mar. 10, 2006. Conflicts with Bell's first telephone call on 03-10.

candidates.title: STS-1 launches the first Space Shuttle
candidates.summary: Space Shuttle Columbia launched on NASA's first shuttle mission with John Young and Robert Crippen aboard. The orbital flight test took a reusable spacecraft system into orbit without a prior uncrewed orbital flight.
candidates.lesson: A reusable vehicle is a system test of structures, propulsion, thermal protection, software and operations at once; flight-test instrumentation must be treated as mission-critical hardware.
candidates.notes: NASA source confirms first Space Shuttle mission and Apr. 12, 1981 launch. Conflicts with Vostok 1 on 04-12.

candidates.title: Mustang turns platform reuse into desire
candidates.summary: Ford introduced the Mustang to the public at the New York World's Fair and in showrooms, packaging familiar components into a new market category.
candidates.lesson: Platform reuse can be innovative when packaging, timing, price and identity are engineered as carefully as the hardware.
candidates.notes: Ford source confirms public introduction on Apr. 17, 1964. Conflicts with West Fertilizer on 04-17.

candidates.title: Rana Plaza turns cracks into a mass-casualty warning
candidates.summary: Rana Plaza in Dhaka, which housed five garment factories, collapsed. At least 1,134 people died and more than 2,500 were injured.
candidates.lesson: Structural warnings must stop occupancy. Production pressure cannot be allowed to override visible damage in a loaded building.
candidates.notes: ILO source confirms Apr. 24, 2013, Dhaka, five garment factories, at least 1,134 deaths and more than 2,500 injuries. Conflicts with Hubble launch on 04-24.

candidates.title: Hindenburg burns during landing
candidates.summary: The German passenger airship Hindenburg caught fire while preparing to land at Lakehurst, New Jersey. The disaster killed 35 people aboard and one member of the ground crew, ending confidence in hydrogen-filled passenger airships.
candidates.lesson: A spectacular vehicle still depends on ordinary operational margins: weather, handling, materials, ignition controls and emergency escape all have to survive the final approach.
candidates.notes: National Archives source confirms May 6, 1937, Lakehurst, and fatalities. Conflicts with Channel Tunnel opening on 05-06. Discipline normalized from Aerospace to Aviation because the production category list does not use Aerospace.

candidates.title: Uster: stainless hangers fail above a pool
candidates.summary: A suspended concrete ceiling collapsed into the indoor pool at Uster, Switzerland, killing 12 people. Chrome-nickel-steel hangers had suffered chloride-driven corrosion and stress-corrosion cracking in the humid pool atmosphere.
candidates.lesson: Stainless is not corrosion-proof. Safety-critical hidden components need material selection and inspection matched to the real atmosphere, not the material's marketing name.
candidates.notes: SRF provides accessible anniversary/context coverage; BGE 115 IV 199 is stronger for technical facts: 207 chrome-nickel-steel hangers, acidic chloride-containing moisture film, pitting, transcrystalline stress-corrosion cracking, overloading, 12 deaths and 19 injured or directly endangered.

candidates.title: Maiman makes the first working laser
candidates.summary: Theodore Maiman switched on a ruby laser at Hughes Research Laboratories, producing the first laser flash. The device turned a laboratory principle into a practical source of coherent light.
candidates.lesson: A breakthrough can come from making a known principle buildable: materials, pumping method, geometry and timing matter as much as the theory.
candidates.source_label: German Patent and Trade Mark Office
candidates.notes: DPMA source confirms May 16, 1960 and Maiman's ruby laser. Conflicts with Ronan Point on 05-16.

candidates.title: Morse sends a message over an electric line
candidates.summary: Samuel Morse sent the first telegraphic message over the experimental Washington-to-Baltimore line. The demonstration showed that coded electrical signals could carry messages over long distance faster than physical transport.
candidates.lesson: A communication breakthrough needs an end-to-end channel, shared encoding and operational proof that the receiver can reconstruct the intended message.
candidates.notes: LOC source confirms May 24, 1844 and first telegraphic message. Conflicts with Brooklyn Bridge opening on 05-24.

candidates.title: Kennedy turns the Moon into a systems deadline
candidates.summary: President John F. Kennedy asked Congress to commit the United States to landing a person on the Moon and returning them safely to Earth before the decade was out.
candidates.lesson: An ambitious engineering program needs a clear outcome, deadline, budget path and system-integration ownership.
candidates.notes: NASA History source confirms Kennedy's May 25, 1961 address and lunar goal. Conflicts with American Airlines Flight 191 on 05-25.

candidates.title: Gemini IV takes an American outside the spacecraft
candidates.summary: NASA's Gemini IV mission launched with James McDivitt and Ed White aboard, and White performed the first American spacewalk. The EVA tested human mobility, tethers and hand-held maneuvering outside the capsule.
candidates.lesson: Working outside a vehicle turns the astronaut, suit, tether, tools and procedures into one life-support system.
candidates.notes: NASA source confirms June 3, 1965 and the first American spacewalk. Conflicts with Therac-25 first overdose on 06-03.

candidates.title: UNIVAC I brings computing into public administration
candidates.summary: Census Bureau officials attended the dedication of UNIVAC I at the Eckert-Mauchly Laboratory in Philadelphia, marking an early commercial computer entering government use.
candidates.lesson: Computing becomes infrastructure when it leaves the lab and attaches to real institutional workloads.
candidates.notes: Census source confirms UNIVAC I dedication on Jun. 14, 1951. Conflicts with Grenfell Tower on 06-14.

candidates.title: SpaceShipOne reaches space privately
candidates.summary: SpaceShipOne became the first privately built and piloted vehicle to reach space. The flight showed that a small experimental team could build, fly and recover a crewed suborbital spacecraft.
candidates.lesson: A smaller program still needs aerospace discipline: incremental tests, abort modes, recovery behavior and pilot workload decide whether bold hardware survives the demo.
candidates.source_label: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
candidates.notes: Smithsonian source confirms June 21, 2004 and first privately built, piloted vehicle to reach space. Conflicts with Manchester Baby on 06-21.

candidates.title: Telstar 1 opens live satellite television
candidates.summary: Telstar 1 launched on a Delta rocket as an active communications satellite able to relay television across the Atlantic. It linked spacecraft, ground stations, antennas and microwave electronics into a working global media system.
candidates.lesson: A communications satellite is only useful when orbit, power, bandwidth, pointing and ground infrastructure all close the link budget together.
candidates.notes: NASA source confirms July 10, 1962 launch and Telstar's role in global satellite television. Conflicts with Seveso on 07-10.

candidates.title: Viking 1 lands and works on Mars
candidates.summary: NASA's Viking 1 lander touched down safely on Mars and began transmitting images from the surface. It became the first truly successful Mars landing and surface mission.
candidates.lesson: A landing milestone matters when touchdown, survivability, communications and useful data return all work together after arrival.
candidates.notes: NASA source confirms July 20, 1976 and first truly successful Mars landing. Conflicts with Apollo 11 on 07-20.

candidates.title: Drake proves oil can be drilled like water
candidates.summary: The Drake Well struck oil near Titusville, Pennsylvania. The successful well helped launch repeatable commercial oil drilling in the United States.
candidates.lesson: A resource boom can start with a production method, not a discovery; repeatable extraction changes the whole system.
candidates.notes: Drake Well Museum source confirms Aug. 27, 1859 and the historic well site. Conflicts with Comair Flight 5191 on 08-27.

candidates.title: A relay fault turns debugging into a record
candidates.summary: A Harvard Mark II team recorded a moth caught between relay contacts and taped it into the computer logbook as the first actual case of a bug being found.
candidates.lesson: Failure records matter. A small fault becomes useful when the system preserves enough context to diagnose and teach it.
candidates.notes: Computer History Museum source confirms Sep. 9, 1947, Harvard Mark II and the logged relay fault. Conflicts with San Bruno pipeline explosion on 09-09.

candidates.title: Luna 2 launches toward the Moon
candidates.summary: The Soviet Union launched Luna 2 on an intercept course with the Moon. The mission became the first human-made object to reach another celestial body when it impacted the lunar surface the next day.
candidates.lesson: A deep-space first can be a one-way proof: navigation, tracking, staging and timing have to be accurate enough even without recovery.
candidates.notes: NASA source confirms Sep. 12, 1959 launch and subsequent lunar impact. Conflicts with Kilby's integrated circuit demonstration on 09-12.

candidates.title: TAT-1 carries telephone calls under the Atlantic
candidates.summary: The first submarine transatlantic telephone cable system went into service, connecting North America and Europe by voice. The system depended on repeaters, cable reliability and shore stations surviving a hostile undersea environment.
candidates.lesson: Long-distance infrastructure succeeds when every hidden element is designed for access limits, environmental exposure and repair reality.
candidates.source_label: IEEE Engineering and Technology History Wiki
candidates.notes: IEEE Milestone source confirms Sep. 25, 1956 service start. Conflicts with PSA Flight 182 on 09-25.

candidates.title: Ford records the first Model T
candidates.summary: Ford's first Model T production card records car number 1 assembled at the Piquette plant in Detroit, a step toward the mass-market automobile system Ford would scale.
candidates.lesson: A revolutionary product still begins as a traceable production object: configuration, records and factory learning make scale possible.
candidates.notes: The Henry Ford source confirms the first Model T was assembled on Sep. 27, 1908. Conflicts with Dawn launch on 09-27.

candidates.title: Tokaido Shinkansen starts high-speed rail service
candidates.summary: The Tokaido Shinkansen opened between Tokyo and Osaka as the world's first high-speed rail service. It treated track, trains, signalling, operations and city-pair demand as one engineered transport system.
candidates.lesson: High speed is not just a faster vehicle; it requires a dedicated alignment, signalling, maintenance and operating model built around the target speed.
candidates.source_label: Embassy of Japan in the UK
candidates.notes: Embassy source confirms Oct. 1, 1964 and world's first high-speed rail service. A JR Central source would be preferable if found later. Conflicts with Sony CDP-101 on 10-01.

candidates.title: Edison's carbon-filament lamp lasts long enough to matter
candidates.summary: Edison's Menlo Park laboratory produced a carbon-filament incandescent lamp that glowed for more than fourteen hours. The result moved electric lighting closer to a practical utility system.
candidates.lesson: The useful invention was not just a glowing filament; it was a manufacturable lamp with lifetime, distribution and system economics moving in the same direction.
candidates.source_label: IEEE Engineering and Technology History Wiki
candidates.notes: IEEE ETHW source confirms Oct. 21, 1879 and the carbonized-thread lamp result. Conflicts with Aberfan on 10-21.

candidates.title: New York opens its first subway line
candidates.summary: The Interborough Rapid Transit subway opened as New York's first underground rapid transit network, with 28 stations over a 9.1-mile route. It converted urban congestion into a large-scale civil, electrical and operating system.
candidates.lesson: Urban transport capacity is engineered as a network: tunnels, stations, signaling, traction power and passenger flow have to scale together.
candidates.notes: Transit Museum source confirms Oct. 27, 1904 opening, station count and route length. Conflicts with nylon announcement on 10-27.

candidates.title: Bhopal: stored MIC escapes into a city
candidates.summary: More than 40 tonnes of methyl isocyanate gas leaked from a pesticide plant in Bhopal, India. Thousands died immediately and the disaster became a defining case in chemical-process safety and emergency preparedness.
candidates.lesson: High-hazard inventory near a city needs independent safeguards, maintainable protection layers, emergency planning and a management system that keeps them alive during shutdown and cost pressure.
candidates.notes: Peer-reviewed review hosted by NIH/PMC confirms Dec. 3, 1984, more than 40 tonnes of MIC, and at least 3,800 immediate deaths. Needs a later source-quality pass for detailed causal wording because official/primary narratives are contested. Conflicts with Mars Polar Lander on 12-03.

candidates.title: Marconi receives a signal across the Atlantic
candidates.summary: Guglielmo Marconi and George Kemp received the first transatlantic radio signals at Signal Hill, Newfoundland. The experiment showed that wireless signals could reach beyond the horizon and across an ocean.
candidates.lesson: A communication claim becomes engineering when propagation, receiver sensitivity, antenna arrangement and repeatable detection all survive the real environment.
candidates.source_label: IEEE Engineering and Technology History Wiki
candidates.notes: IEEE Milestone source confirms Dec. 12, 1901 at Signal Hill. Conflicts with Clapham Junction on 12-12.

candidates.title: Mitholz: stored ammunition remains an active system
candidates.summary: Part of the ammunition stored in the Swiss Army's underground Mitholz depot exploded, killing nine people and damaging the village. Thousands of tonnes of munition remnants remain a long-term clearance and risk-management problem.
candidates.lesson: Hazardous storage does not become safe because it is abandoned or buried. Inventory, degradation, confinement, water ingress and future access remain engineering responsibilities for decades.
candidates.notes: The explosion occurred during the night of 19/20 December 1947. Stored as 12-19 for now because armasuisse states December 1947 and other sources identify 19 December; 12-20 is also occupied by EBR-I.

candidates.title: Bell Labs demonstrates the transistor
candidates.summary: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain demonstrated the point-contact transistor to Bell Labs supervisors, turning solid-state amplification into a working device.
candidates.lesson: A component-level breakthrough can redraw whole systems when it changes size, reliability, power and manufacturability at once.
candidates.notes: Computer History Museum source confirms Dec. 23, 1947 demonstration to Bell Labs supervisors. Conflicts with first successful kidney transplant on 12-23.
